answer: A new node always enters at the bottom-most, left-most open spot, which sits under 7, not 9. Once 3 is there, it only compares against its direct parent as it bubbles up.
5 keeps moving because it's larger than its neighbors, so it bubbles up until it hits a larger number or the end of the list.
Gravity constantly pulls the vertical velocity downward while horizontal velocity stays constant, bending the straight line into a parabola.

If water were linear at 180°, the two lone pairs and two bonds would be tightly cramped on one side. By bending to 104.5°, the four electron pairs get as far apart from each other as possible in three-dimensional space.
